llm_narrative: Across the 500 evaluation tasks, cogito_3b_output achieved a mean claim‑coverage of only 0.0413 (≈4 % of ground‑truth statements), a median coverage of 0 and a 0.75‑threshold pass rate of 20 %, indicating that most responses failed to satisfy even a single required claim. The dominant failure modes were omission of tool usage (251 instances, 50.2 % of all tasks) followed by task misunderstanding (114, 22.8 %) and early termination (105, 21.0 %), which together account for more than 90 % of the errors. Although 257 tasks (51.4 %) did involve at least one tool call, the overall tool‑call versus pure‑cognitive split (257 vs 243) shows that merely invoking a tool does not guarantee success; the majority of missed claims still stem from downstream cognitive failures such as mis‑parsing outputs or aborting before synthesis. A concrete remediation is to enforce a post‑tool‑call validation step—e.g., a lightweight verifier that checks whether all required tool results have been incorporated into the final answer and, if not, prompts the model to retrieve missing data before concluding. What sets cogito_3b_output apart from other models is that its error profile is driven almost entirely by procedural omissions (no_tool_use, early exit) rather than hallucinated facts or incorrect synthesis, suggesting a systemic weakness in managing multi‑step tool workflows.
